newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine senators plan Falkland war graves visit.
newsitem.headline: Argentine senators plan Falkland war graves visit.

text.p: A group of Argentine senators led by President Carlos Menem's brother Eduardo said on Thursday they wanted to travel to the Falkland Islands to visit the graves of Argentine soldiers killed in the 1982 war.
"I think the time has come for the representatives of the people to pay homage to them in the place where their bodies lay," said Eduardo Menem, head of the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee.

Argentine passport holders generally are not allowed to visit the Falklands. Since the war, in which Britain ousted Argentine troops trying to enforce a 130-year-old sovereignty claim, fiercely pro-British islanders have allowed only five grave visits by relatives of fallen Argentine soldiers.
The latest visits, by two small groups of mourners, were in January and February.

But Menem said Argentine lawmakers should be given access to the windswept cemetery near Darwin and Goose Green, scene of some of the worst fighting of the 10-week war. The cemetery contains the graves of 234 Argentine servicemen, many identified only as "Conscript" or "Soldier."
The rest of the Argentine war dead were lost at sea. The known death toll for the war was 652 Argentines and 255 British servicemen.
Menem said he would ask the Argentine Foreign Ministry to negotiate the visit with London, but insisted this "does not mean asking permission."

At the British embassy in Buenos Aires, a spokesman said Britain "has received no proposal for such a visit from the Argentine government. Any decision on access to the Falklands is a matter for the Falkland Islands councilors."

The governor of the province of Entre Rios, Jorge Busti, visited the British embassy in Buenos Aires last month to seek clearance to visit the graves in the name of relatives of 32 Entre Rios men who died in the war. He was told the Falklands government does not issue entry visas.
